name: Agamand Family Mace
summary: At Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Mace remains locked in the family crypt. Once a proud heirloom of northern Lordaeron, it is now sought by their former servant, Coleman Farthing.

sections.title: A Legacy in Ruin
sections.body: Before the Third War, the Agamand family held vast farmlands and windmills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Like the region’s other aristocrats, they fell to the plague of undeath. The Scourge raised them as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, and they wander their ruined estate. Their ancient treasures remain locked in the family crypt. Among them rests the Agamand Family Mace, a remnant of a lineage reduced to shambling undead.

sections.title: A Servant's Vengeance
sections.body: Coleman Farthing seeks the mace along with three other martial heirlooms. The former Agamand employee blames the family for his death. Raised among the Forsaken, Farthing wants to strip the mindless Agamands of every trace of dignity and honor. He seeks the ancestral sword, axe, and dagger as well as the mace, hoping to erase the memory and pride of his former masters from the lands they once ruled.

faq.q: Where is the Agamand Family Mace located?
faq.answer: The mace rests on a weapon rack inside the Agamand Family Crypt, at the far northern end of Agamand Mills in Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Who wants the Agamand Family Mace?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken living in Brill, demands the mace and the other family heirlooms to settle an old score with his former masters.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want the heirlooms stolen?
faq.answer: Farthing served the Agamands in life and blames them for his death. Taking their prized weapons from the crypt is his way of erasing the last traces of their family honor.

faq.q: What happened to the Agamand family?
faq.answer: The Agamand family ruled the prosperous Agamand Mills in northern Lordaeron until the plague struck. Their reanimated corpses now wander the estate and crypts as mindless thralls of the Scourge.

angles.text: The desecration of the Agamand crypts shows how old mortal grievances can drive the Forsaken to settle scores from life.
